body:
@stuartwdouglas We can fix that by checking whether or not the application is producing its own tenant configuration.

The reason why a thread pool is being used is that the configuration can be built in a blocking way.

@sberyozkin both `TenantConfigResolver` and `TenantResolver`. The reason for the latter is that I'm not sure if people will respect the non-blocking behavior all the time. But in theory, we could have a check only for `TenantConfigResolver`.

It is fine to check `TenantConfigResolver` only. I was more concerned about corner cases where the `TenantResolver` could potentially perform a more costly operation even though it just resolves the tenant identifier (e.g.: due to unknown reasons invoke some service to decide the tenant, etc).

Could you elaborate more about tweaking `TenantConfigResolver` ?
All makes sense. Will update things accordingly.

@sberyozkin Btw, in regards to changing `CompletableFuture<OidcTenantConfig>` from the main resolver. We only have access to `AuthenticationRequestContext.runBlocking(Supplier<SecurityIdentity> function)` so that we can run any blocking code. We need to do it differently, I would just add a `isBlocking` method to the `DefaultTenantConfigResolver` and check it when authenticating from `OidcIdentityProvider`.

Or do you see any other better option ?
